title: Describe a person who tells interesting stories.
bullets: where you usually hear their stories
what their stories are usually about
explain: and explain why you enjoy listening to them.
followUps: Do you ever try to retell their stories to friends?
p3: What makes a story worth listening to the second time?
How has the way people share stories changed over the last few decades?
In what ways do stories help people understand those who are different from them?
What separates natural storytellers from people who struggle to hold an audience?
How do families pass down their history through the stories they tell at home?
Would a community lose something important if its traditional tales were no longer told?

title: Describe a guest who came to stay with your family.
bullets: how long they stayed with you
what you did together during the visit
explain: and explain whether the visit turned out the way you had hoped.
followUps: Would you be happy to host a guest like that again?
p3: What do people in many countries expect from a host when a visitor stays under their roof?
How does staying with friends or relatives differ from staying in a hotel?
Why do some families find it hard to welcome visitors for a long period?
Has the growth of cheap hotels and holiday rentals changed the custom of hosting guests?
How might the custom of hosting guests change as homes become smaller in crowded cities?
Would a society become less friendly if people stopped inviting visitors into their homes?

title: Describe a person who gives excellent talks or speeches.
bullets: where they usually give their talks
what makes their talks so effective
explain: and explain why their talks have had such an effect on you.
followUps: Would you enjoy giving a talk to a large audience?
p3: What kinds of people are most often asked to give speeches in public?
What makes so many people nervous about speaking in front of a large audience?
How does a good speech differ from a good piece of writing?
Are speeches still influential in an age of short videos and online posts?
How might the way people listen to speeches change as more of them are recorded and shared online?
Will confident public speaking become less valued in the jobs of the future?

title: Describe a mountain or hill you have climbed or visited.
bullets: what the climb or visit involved
explain: and explain what made the effort feel worthwhile.
followUps: Would you climb it again if you had the chance?
p3: What draws so many people to walk in the hills at weekends?
What are the main risks people face when they go walking in mountain country?
How do mountain regions differ from flat areas in the way their people live and work?
Is it right to limit the number of visitors to fragile natural areas?
How might tourism change the character of remote mountain villages over time?
Could climbing become a less popular pastime if the weather in high places grows less predictable?

title: Describe a small town or village you have been to.
bullets: what you did while you were there
explain: and explain how it made you feel.
followUps: Would you enjoy living somewhere as peaceful as that?
p3: What are the main advantages of living in a small community rather than a large city?
Why do many young people leave villages for bigger towns when they finish school?
What role do local shops and cafes play in holding a small community together?
Does a rise in tourism always help a quiet village, or can it cause problems too?
How might fast internet access change the future of rural areas?
What effect could remote working have on the population of small towns?

title: Describe an underground or metro system you have used.
bullets: what made it easy or difficult to use
explain: and explain whether you think it works well as a model for other cities.
followUps: Do you usually prefer trains to buses in a city?
p3Topics: Cost and design of underground railways
p3: What problems do large cities face when they try to keep their transport running smoothly?
How do underground railways compare with buses in terms of speed and carrying capacity?
Why are some metro systems far more crowded than others in the same city?
Is it wise for a city to spend huge sums on new underground lines when cheaper options exist?
How could an underground network shape the way a city grows over several decades?
What trade-off do cities face between building new lines and maintaining the existing ones?

title: Describe a pair of shoes you liked a lot.
explain: and explain why they meant so much to you.
followUps: How many pairs of shoes do you usually own?
p3: What do people in most countries look for when they buy a new pair of shoes?
How has buying clothes changed with the growth of online shopping?
Why do some people spend a lot on fashion while others prefer plain, practical clothes?
Are fashion trends spreading faster now than they did a generation ago?
How much can clothing reveal about a person's personality or background?
Will fast fashion stay popular if more people become concerned about the waste it creates?

title: Describe a present you gave to someone.
bullets: how they reacted when they opened it
explain: and explain why you chose this particular present.
followUps: Do you enjoy choosing presents for other people?
p3: Which occasions tend to call for a present in most countries?
What makes some people prefer giving experiences, such as a meal out, to giving objects?
How do expensive gifts compare with thoughtful but inexpensive ones in the eyes of the receiver?
Is gift giving becoming more about obligation than about generosity?
How might the custom of giving presents change as more people shop online?
What effect does gift giving have on relationships between friends and within families?

title: Describe a piece of equipment you used at school.
bullets: how it helped with your studies
explain: and explain how useful you found it.
followUps: Did the other pupils use it as much as you did?
p3: What kinds of equipment do schools need most in order to teach science well?
How important is up-to-date equipment compared with having good teachers?
Why do some schools struggle to afford new equipment for their pupils?
What are the advantages and drawbacks of replacing printed textbooks with tablets?
How has classroom technology changed the way children learn to read and write?
Could schools one day rely entirely on digital equipment, or would something important be lost?

title: Describe a school sports day or open day you remember.
bullets: who took part and who came to watch
explain: and explain why it still means so much to you.
followUps: Do you think schools should hold events like this more often?
p3: What purpose do school events serve beyond the classroom?
Compared with other ways of building community, what do sports days contribute?
What makes some pupils dislike competitive events, even when they are good at sport?
Does competition at a young age encourage children to work harder, or does it discourage them?
How might the balance between competition and cooperation at school shape adults' attitudes to work?
How much weight do schools tend to give to results compared with taking part?

title: Describe a festival from another country that you would like to experience.
explain: and explain why you would like to see it for yourself.
followUps: Do you know anyone who has already been to it?
p3: What kinds of festivals attract the most visitors from other countries?
What leads so many people to travel abroad for local celebrations?
Can a centuries-old festival offer anything that a modern music festival cannot?
Is there a risk that a festival loses its authenticity once it attracts large crowds?
How can communities keep their old customs alive as young people move away to the cities?
What role could festivals play in helping different cultures understand one another?

title: Describe a time when you tried something new and did not succeed at first.
bullets: what happened in those early attempts
explain: and explain how you dealt with the disappointment.
followUps: Did you eventually manage to master it?
p3: What is the real value of a first attempt that goes badly?
How do attitudes to failure differ between schools and workplaces?
What keeps some people from trying new things altogether?
Is it wiser to stay with a skill you already have than to begin learning a new one?
How does a culture's view of mistakes affect the way children learn?
Will people become more willing to take risks as more learning moves online?

title: Describe a time when you had to make an important phone call.
explain: and explain how you prepared for it beforehand.
followUps: Do you find phone calls harder than sending messages?
p3: How has the telephone changed the way people communicate in business?
What lies behind many people's nervousness about calling strangers?
What are the main differences between a phone call and a face-to-face meeting?
Are text messages replacing phone calls, and is that a good development?
How might the role of the telephone change as voice assistants improve?
What effect does constant messaging have on people's ability to hold a long conversation?

title: Describe a time when you made a promise to someone.
bullets: how you kept or broke it
explain: and explain why this promise was so important to you.
followUps: Is it hard to say no when someone asks you for a promise?
p3: What does it mean for people to be considered trustworthy in everyday life?
How important is trust in a close friendship compared with a working relationship?
Why are promises sometimes harder to keep than people expect when they make them?
Would a society function well if people stopped trusting one another's word?
How do written contracts differ from spoken promises in building trust?
Can a culture that values honesty above all still leave people room to change their minds?

title: Describe a holiday that did not go as planned.
explain: and explain how you made the best of it.
followUps: Would you go back to the same place?
p3: What kinds of problems do travellers most often run into while on holiday?
How does planning a trip in detail differ from simply going with the flow?
Why do some people find it hard to relax when things do not go to plan?
Are package holidays less likely to go wrong than independent travel?
How might travel insurance and booking technology change people's expectations of a holiday?
If holidays became less predictable, what effect would that have on the travel industry?

title: Describe a dance or exercise class you have taken.
bullets: what type of class it was
explain: and explain whether you would recommend it to others.
followUps: Would you go back to a class like that if you had the chance?
p3: What draws people to group exercise classes rather than working out alone?
In what ways do dance classes compare with gym workouts for fitness?
Why do some people give up on exercise after only a few weeks?
Are fitness trends such as dance workouts likely to last, or will they fade?
How has the rise of home exercise videos changed the way people stay fit?
To what extent could public health improve if group exercise were cheaper and easier to join?

title: Describe a hobby you would recommend to older people.
explain: and explain why you think it suits people later in life.
followUps: Do you have a hobby you started only recently?
p3Topics: Learning new skills at any age
p3: What are the main benefits of having a hobby once people have retired?
How do quiet pastimes such as gardening differ from more active hobbies like swimming?
What leaves some older people feeling isolated, and how can hobbies help?
Is it realistic to expect people in later life to take up demanding new activities?
How might a larger number of retired people with free time affect local leisure services?
What effect could lifelong learning have on how long people stay healthy and independent?

title: Describe a task you find difficult but worth doing.
explain: and explain why you keep going with it.
followUps: Do you think people should always finish what they start?
p3: What kinds of tasks do people usually find hardest to stick with over a long period?
How do people keep themselves motivated when a task starts to feel boring?
Why do some people give up on long projects while others keep going to the end?
Is the satisfaction of finishing something hard always greater than the pleasure of an easy success?
To what extent does a culture's respect for effort shape how children approach difficult work?
Could more emphasis on patience in schools produce adults who are more resilient in the long run?

title: Describe a TV series you watched from start to finish.
bullets: how you came to watch it
explain: and explain why you decided to watch the whole thing.
followUps: Do you usually watch several episodes in a row?
p3: What makes people choose to watch a long series in one go rather than week by week?
How have streaming services changed the way television drama is made?
What makes some programmes become talking points across an entire country?
Is television still a shared experience, or do people now watch alone on their own schedules?
How might the way families watch television together change in the future?
What effect does an almost endless choice of programmes have on the attention given to any single one?

title: Describe a play or musical you have seen.
bullets: where and when you saw it
explain: and explain how it affected you.
followUps: Would you like to see another musical soon?
p3: What makes many people prefer live performances to recordings of them?

What are the main challenges facing small theatres in towns and cities?

How might theatre change as audiences grow used to watching performances on screens?
What role could a local theatre play in bringing a community together?
